newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy's Stet to unveil merger details Friday.
newsitem.headline: Italy's Stet to unveil merger details Friday.

text.p: Italian state telecommunications holding Stet said on Wednesday it would unveil long-awaited details of the merger with its main operating unit, Telecom Italia, after a board meeting on Friday.

A company spokesman said the group's 1996 results and details of the so-called industrial plan which will set out the structure of the new merged entity would be released after the meeting in Rome ended in the early afternoon.
Stet and Telecom Italia shareholders gave their approval to the merger at an extraordinary meeting on April 30,
The link-up between two big players on the world telecoms stage -- Telecom Italia is the world's sixth biggest operator by number of subscribers -- aims to create a single national force.

The merger is a preliminary step in the long-delayed privatisation of Stet. Prime Minister Romano Prodi's centre-left government wants to complete the sale by the year-end, pending parliamentary approval of a regulatory watchdog for the sector.

Stet managing director Tomaso Tommasi di Vignano told a parliamentary commission last month that he wanted the industrial plan to set out four objectives -- to defend the home market with cost cuts, to boost cellphone services, to increase multimedia development and to expand activities abroad.
As global telecoms alliances flourish, Tommasi also said the group needed to find an international partner.
The company created by the merger will keep the name Telecom Italia and will become operational on July 18. Its shares will start trading the next day.

The Stet spokesman said Friday's meeting would also name the director general of the merged company and other management, as well as addressing a range of business issues including whether the sale of cable making unit Sirti would go ahead.
Other issues concerned Stet's multimedia unit Stream and its fibre-optic cabling project, he said.

Stet said a month ago that it had not yet set a date for the Sirti disposal, but newspapers have suggested a sale could take place by the summer. Stet is due to put on the market its 48.9 percent stake in Sirti which is already quoted in Milan.

The board meeting will also release Stet's full 1996 results. The group has already reported that net profit last year was 1.11 trillion lire ($652 million). $1 = 1,702 lire -- Rome newsroom +396 678 2501
